issues.description: Inlining full compiled script into every compile RPC response is the wrong shape.
issues.detail: The backend already wrote the file to disk and returns its path, yet stuffs the full contents into every compile_notebook response. This bloats memory and bandwidth for a payload only sometimes used, and complects 'where the artifact lives' with 'what it is'. Add a dedicated download RPC or serve the file by path, fetched on demand.

issues.description: open() lacks encoding and error handling, so a post-success read failure poisons the compile result.
issues.detail: open(script_path) uses platform-default encoding with no try/except. If the file is missing, unreadable, or non-utf8, the entire compile_notebook RPC fails after compilation succeeded. Specify encoding='utf-8', handle IOError separately from compile failure, or remove the read entirely.

issues.description: Download button renders unconditionally; missing compiledContent yields a silent no-op click.
issues.detail: handleDownloadClick guards on compiledPath && compiledContent and returns silently on failure, but the icon renders in the success branch regardless. With an older backend or partial response, the user clicks and nothing happens with no feedback. Gate rendering on compiledContent or show a disabled state.

issues.description: GetAppIcon is used as a click target instead of a real button.
issues.detail: The SVG icon has onClick and titleAccess but no button element, no keyboard handler, no role, and no focus ring. The adjacent 'Done' link is a proper anchor. Wrap in IconButton or use <a download href={objectUrl}> to match accessibility expectations and surrounding code style.

issues.description: Filename derivation conflates the package path with the .py script artifact and uses a misleading fallback.
issues.detail: compiledPath points at the pipeline package while the download writes script_content (.py), with a fallback to 'pipeline.kale.py' when the path is empty. Two different values are addressed by one identity. Either name them distinctly (scriptPath vs packagePath) or guarantee the path is non-empty and remove the fallback.

issues.description: Imperative anchor-click DOM dance with fragile object URL lifecycle.
issues.detail: createElement, appendChild, click, removeChild, revokeObjectURL expresses one fact via six mutation steps, and revoke happens inline after click() so it leaks if click throws or the component unmounts mid-flight. Prefer a declarative <a download href={objectUrl}> with explicit useEffect cleanup, or eliminate the Blob path entirely by fetching the served file.

synthesis.summary: NEEDS-WORK. The panel agrees the feature works but the shape is wrong: the backend inlines the entire compiled script into every compile RPC response when a path-based download endpoint would suffice, and the file read has no encoding or error handling so a post-success IOError poisons the whole compile result. On the frontend, the download icon renders unconditionally with a silent no-op fallback, is an SVG with onClick instead of a real button, and uses an imperative anchor-click DOM dance with a fragile object URL lifecycle. Good taste here is eliminating the special case: one path, fetched when clicked, rendered as a proper accessible control.
